faults.trigger: AC, GM20B, 0x000b000f, two-buffer SEQUENTIAL window, no application writes, first Present(1,0).
faults.cause: Historical initiating failure unknown. Each of the three original boots ended abnormally after the first Present call marker. The readable graphics streams end before that marker. A later instrumented trial directly observed the ordinary-context staging copy rejection. A one-time functional candidate completed the same native scene on three consecutive runs, with GPU copy retirement, verified window output, input, normal exit and desktop continuity. The historical crash boundary lacks a comparable DDI receipt or dump.
faults.daily_workaround: Keep this native Blt path out of daily launches. A client with a validated flip option may use the verified legacy FLIP_SEQUENTIAL route within its tested scope. The six-frame control matched 15 desktop samples. The WARP empty-window control is a separate software result.
faults.close_when: Identify the initiating failure and fix it. Retest the original legacy SEQUENTIAL trigger on AC at least three consecutive times, including correct visible output, normal exit and desktop continuity.

faults.trigger: Process-scoped WDDM 2.0 interface 0x000b0020, first empty Present on SEQUENTIAL or FLIP_SEQUENTIAL.
faults.cause: The runtime supplied Reserved=1 and the Present1 input guard returned E_INVALIDARG before the Windows callback. In the process-scoped candidate, the identical FLIP_SEQUENTIAL empty window reached the callback and returned S_OK. A one-clear window also returned S_OK and matched all five desktop samples. The other swap effect still needs candidate validation.
faults.daily_workaround: Keep the experimental WDDM 2.0 offer confined to a one-time diagnostic client. Use only application paths with independent physical acceptance for daily use.
faults.close_when: Verify actual rendering, on-screen output and normal exit through the affected system swap effects on three consecutive trials. Keep the legacy restart open until its own criteria pass.

faults.trigger: A six-frame native WDDM 2.0 window with external power and the process-scoped Present1 correction. Two frames returned successfully before an unexpected restart.
faults.cause: Unknown. The last durable application record entered the third Present. The captured DXGI trace ended 8.643 ms before that entry. Windows reported Kernel-Power 41 with bugcheck zero and event 6008, without a matching shutdown intent. The dump inventory was unchanged.
faults.daily_workaround: Keep multi-frame rendering through the process-scoped WDDM 2.0 candidate in diagnostics. The previous legacy FLIP_SEQUENTIAL six-frame control is qualified only for its measured client and scene.
faults.close_when: Identify and repair the initiating fault. Run the original multi-frame scene on external power at least three consecutive times with the tested components, verified display samples, normal exit and a continuous desktop.

faults.trigger: Intermittent desktop, game, video, exit or file-operation loads. Published observations have different trigger and power conditions.
faults.cause: Unknown. A common initiating failure across these observations has not been established.
faults.daily_workaround: Keep unqualified heavy-load paths in diagnostics. Use only a previously accepted alternative for the specific application and workload. No universal game or extraction workaround has been verified.
faults.close_when: Separate triggers with identified causes and document a fix and three consecutive original-scenario retests for each remaining restart.

faults.trigger: Wi-Fi driver failed to start on a boot reported by the operator, followed by a manual restart.
faults.cause: Startup cause unknown. The manual restart is documented separately from graphics resets.
faults.daily_workaround: Use confirmed working connectivity for remote operation. Keep startup reliability out of acceptance until it is tested.
faults.close_when: Identify the startup failure and qualify the corrected driver on repeated Windows boots with actual network access.

faults.trigger: Accepted ARM64 tgd3d 57dc16b4 on GM20B, legacy DXGI Blt1, sRGB source and UNORM destination. The identical test on optimal images changed all 88 pixels in a rectangular copy and all 748 interior pixels in a scaled channel conversion.
faults.cause: The unrotated path uses a Vulkan image blit that decodes sRGB channel values during conversion to UNORM. The signed candidate retained the encoded values on the same hardware and executable. The three logged empty sequential restarts used UNORM application buffers.
faults.daily_workaround: In a client that can choose its copy route, the accepted driver passed the measured one-to-one B8G8R8A8_UNORM copy between optimal surfaces. Keep sRGB-to-UNORM presentation copies in diagnostics for clients without a separately qualified option.
faults.close_when: On candidate components eligible for presentation promotion, repeat the original encoded-region and filtered-channel cases on AC in three consecutive runs. Verify pixel values, untouched borders, normal exit and the desktop. Record the adopted source, loaded component hashes and actual presentation output.

resolution.root_cause: A Vulkan blit decoded encoded sRGB when DXGI required preserved channel bytes. The same signed comparator distinguished the baseline and corrected production driver on GM20B.

faults.trigger: During restoration from a one-use display KMD to the previously accepted seven-file profile, Windows began the requested native boot 84914. It started again 47.020 seconds later as 84936, with no second shutdown request or game launch in the recorded sequence.
faults.cause: Unknown. System events 41 and 6008 report the abnormal shutdown. The bugcheck and power button timestamp were zero; no dump was written in the observed interval. Driver activation and DWM on the interrupted boot were not independently observed.
faults.daily_workaround: Keep the accepted signed profile and its Code 43 recovery path available. After a necessary recovery, check the most recent boot ID, Code 0, loaded components and compositor before starting a graphics workload. These checks verified the recovered desktop on boot 84936. A preventive workaround remains open.
faults.close_when: Identify the initiating cause on the native recovery boot. After repair, repeat the same controlled return to the accepted profile on AC at least three consecutive times without an extra boot; confirm the login/desktop, Code 0, loaded component hashes and a normal window exit.

faults.trigger: Native FLIP_SEQUENTIAL swap chain, BGRA8, fixed 90-degree desktop. Request exclusive mode with SetFullscreenState(TRUE, explicit output).
faults.cause: The miniport enumerated only its POST X8R8G8B8 surface format. The measured Windows CDD discarded format 22 while building the GDI list. DXGI could find the native timing but its ChangeDisplaySettingsExW fullscreen request failed before the client UMD mode callback. Enumerating the supported A8R8G8B8 format alongside POST fixed the same signed exclusive client.
faults.daily_workaround: Before this repair the ordinary flip window and a full-monitor borderless window displayed and exited reliably in their measured controls.
faults.close_when: On the one-use fixed Code 0 boot, the original exclusive client must acquire ownership, show three frames, process input, release ownership and return to the same desktop on three consecutive launches.

resolution.root_cause: The miniport enumerated only its POST X8R8G8B8 surface format. The measured Windows CDD discarded format 22 while building the GDI list. DXGI could find the native timing but its ChangeDisplaySettingsExW fullscreen request failed before the client UMD mode callback. Enumerating the supported A8R8G8B8 format alongside POST fixed the same signed exclusive client.

faults.trigger: Conditions before the interruption are only partly known. Boot 85471 recorded Windows resource exhaustion, then boot 85554 began before any workload in this fourth-step chat.
faults.cause: Unknown. System event 2004 recorded 5964984320 of 6118985728 bytes committed, including 4486160384 bytes for powershell.exe. The subsequent 41 had zero BugcheckCode and 6008 reported abnormal shutdown. No intervening 1074 or new dump was observed. The process identity and memory pressure alone do not explain the reset.
faults.daily_workaround: After an interruption, read the boot events and verify the selected seven-file profile, compositor, Code 0 and power before starting graphics work. Limit diagnostic queries to the relevant records. A preventive workaround for this incident is unverified.
faults.close_when: Identify the workload and initiating cause, correct it, and verify three consecutive runs under the original conditions with adequate commit headroom, normal exit and a continuous desktop.

faults.trigger: Interactive desktop restart request on accepted-profile boot 86993, before step-four candidate deployment.
faults.cause: RuntimeBroker requested a restart in the interactive user session. Winlogon and EventLog began shutdown. The subsequent 6008 and 41 reported an abnormal shutdown with bugcheck zero. The initiating restart request is identified. The failure to complete shutdown cleanly is unresolved.
faults.daily_workaround: After a desktop restart, verify the boot record, Code 0, compositor, accepted component hashes and power. A preventive measure is unverified.
faults.close_when: Identify the interrupted shutdown stage, correct the initiating fault and verify three consecutive equivalent desktop restarts with clean shutdown records and an accepted-profile desktop.

faults.trigger: First normal legacy SEQUENTIAL window copy from the application render context into its standard staging surface.
faults.cause: The miniport accepted the requested Blt only on a GDI context and returned STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED to the normal application context. Windows reported occlusion and queued no copy for this window.
faults.daily_workaround: Retain the previously working flip-window path on older builds.
faults.close_when: The original native application presents a visible window, handles input, exits and returns to the same desktop in three consecutive runs. Check a previously working native flip window on the candidate.

resolution.root_cause: Plain Blt on a non-GDI rendering context returns STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED.

faults.trigger: An accepted-stack process-scoped WDDM 2.0 flip control was issued on boot 87614. The client has no retained result. Boot 87687 recorded events 6008 and 41.
faults.cause: Unconfirmed. Available records do not establish whether the client reached Present1 or whether this shares a cause with earlier restarts.
faults.daily_workaround: Keep the optional process-scoped WDDM 2.0 Present1 test deferred. Use the selected native ordinary-window path.
faults.close_when: Identify the cause with retained evidence specific to this incident and verify the corresponding repaired path.

faults.trigger: Read-only device return on boot 88248 exposed additional abnormal-shutdown records following the previously documented boot 87687, before the new GDI dispatch. Boot 90934 also reports an abnormal end to the unobserved boot 90872, after the earlier PAL4 test on boot 90785 had ended in a user-confirmed shutdown.
faults.cause: Unconfirmed. The retained records do not correlate these events to a driver candidate, application, or specific initiating load.
faults.daily_workaround: After a restart, verify Code 0, the active compositor and the selected signed component hashes before resuming the workload.
faults.close_when: Identify the initiating scenarios and causes, and retain matching clean reproduction evidence for a fix.

independence.reason: The startup callback samples only the miniport startup stage. The tested patch leaves presentation, Present1, and GPU scheduling code untouched. The one-use GM20B desktop passed its original GDI output, native texture import, input, and exit controls.

The startup callback samples only the miniport startup stage. The tested patch leaves presentation, Present1, and GPU scheduling code untouched. The one-use GM20B desktop passed its original GDI output, native texture import, input, and exit controls.

The startup callback samples only the miniport startup stage. The tested patch leaves presentation, Present1, and GPU scheduling code untouched. The one-use GM20B desktop passed its original GDI output, native texture import, input, and exit controls.
No load, clock, storage or submission policy changes. The GM20B one-use desktop reproduced the baseline GDI client lifecycle.
No network or Wi-Fi driver changes. The device reconnected during the controlled sequence and returned the native desktop evidence.

The actual Windows STARTDEVICE callback sampled the existing closed-gate failure without changing it. The signed candidate also booted at Code 0 after a controlled restart. This evidence leaves the historic recovery restart open.
The diagnostic wrote 20 bytes in Windows-owned storage without allocating a private buffer. No change to application memory or graphics allocation policy.
The startup observer does not participate in desktop shutdown. The qualification interval pairs each restart with Windows shutdown intent and clean EventLog stop.

The startup callback samples only the miniport startup stage. The tested patch leaves presentation, Present1, and GPU scheduling code untouched. The one-use GM20B desktop passed its original GDI output, native texture import, input, and exit controls.
The earlier events predate this test. The isolated callback and normal Code 0 desktop cases ran within a separate clean Windows event interval.

The previous empty native UNORM case reached the user-mode dispatch of D3DKMT_PRESENT. Its kernel trace ended before the origin of the restart was identified. This release keeps the legacy Present callback, KMD, NVK and runtime fence implementation. Both exact model status queries and unchanged presentation counts were verified on the candidate. Real native sequential submission remains excluded from daily use; no repair is claimed. The candidate passed the separate ordinary Blt outputs and visible flip control.

The registered incident uses the optional 0x000b0020 client and third-frame sequence. The release retains the ordinary interface negotiation. Its supported native legacy flip window displayed its reference and exited; the experimental multi-frame case remains in diagnostics.

The process-scoped WDDM 2.0 offer and Present1 Reserved guard are outside this copy repair. Public device/context creation and drawing passed through the ordinary selected driver; the experimental offer is not enabled by the candidate.

The KMD, NVK and CPU/GPU/EMC scheduling binaries are unchanged. This candidate completed the seven native copy, overlap and pending-write cases and returned to the same desktop. The broader load fault remains open and no universal stability claim is made.
The Wi-Fi package and startup path are unchanged. The externally powered candidate remained connected and the real native color conversion reached verified desktop RGB and normal exit.

The registered empty legacy SEQUENTIAL client last reached D3DKMT_PRESENT, with the subsequent kernel failure still unresolved. The diagnosed fullscreen failure instead occurs in Win32 mode enumeration before exclusive submission. The target fixed mode and row-scan allocations keep their existing pitch. A separate ordinary flip window and the earlier NULL/rotated-storage contract records are retained.

The earlier extra boot occurred during restoration of the old selected kernel, before any fullscreen client had run. Its kernel identity and exact cause on that interrupted boot remain unknown. This candidate had one correlated external-power Code 0 start and no additional boot or TDR in the measured interval while the exclusive clients ran. The earlier incident remains open.

The reported third-frame restart is on the optional 0x000b0020 path. Here the release uses the ordinary negotiated path with the same signed UMD and NVK. Its ordinary flip desktop output, borderless frames, input and exit were measured.
The release keeps the selected UMD and its default legacy DDI. This fixes the Win32 display mode list. The optional WDDM 2.0 callback removal remains outside these successful exclusive frames.

The candidate changes display-mode enumeration and two checked display contracts. The release retains the CPU, GPU and EMC policies and submission queue. The observed exclusive frames completed on AC within the same boot. General load-induced restarts stay open.
The Wi-Fi driver and boot configuration were unchanged. The candidate boot connected and the normal-window control returned to the same available desktop.
